title: I Reported the Cabin Key Log After the Reset Weekend

parts.text: I hung the cabin key on the woodstove hook and saw a second green rubber head already hanging. We had paid for a reset weekend after nine years with Evan, who made coffee too sweet lately, like a test. I am twenty-six, kitchen-table designer. The A-frame smelled like wet dog though no dog was allowed. Evan dropped the grocery bags. "Cute," he said. I opened the binder with Wi-Fi passwords and an entry log. Last line: yesterday, 4:10 p.m., initials E.M., note extra towels. We arrived today at 6:02. Evan Miles. I held the binder. "You were here yesterday?" He rearranged yogurt in the fridge. "The company sent me early. Surprise." Two wine glasses sat in the sink with dull berry lipstick I do not wear. I wear mint ChapStick that stings. "Evan." He shut the fridge. "Don't start. You wanted a reset." I found a cheap black hair tie with a gold bead on the nightstand. "Housekeeping," he said. "Housekeeping initials E.M.?" He grabbed for the binder. I stepped onto the deck. Lake like black glass. One bar of signal. I photographed the log, the glasses, the cologne bottle I had not packed. Evan said, "If you send that, you're choosing war." I sent it to myself. Then the motion light slammed on. Gravel popped. A car I did not recognize came up the drive at 6:19, and Evan whispered, "Don't.".
parts.cliffhanger_hint: A second car is on the gravel, the log proves he was here yesterday, and he just called the photos war.

social.video_title: The cabin log said he arrived yesterday — Part 1/2
social.description: A reset weekend, two wine glasses, and initials that did not match check-in. Someone was coming up the drive. Would you have stayed on the deck?

parts.text: The sedan crunched to a stop and Tasha got out with berry lipstick. She froze. "Oh. I thought you two were—" Evan talked over her. "Tasha from the office. Towels." Tasha looked at the second hook, then at me. "I don't work for the office." The wet-dog smell had a jacket. I stayed on the damp deck because the wood was real. I said, "The log says extra towels at 4:10 yesterday." Tasha laughed once, hurt. "He told me you weren't coming until Sunday." It was Saturday. I packed my duffel and left the ChapStick on the binder so I would not be a ghost. Evan blocked the door. "We can talk." I said, "Talk to the log." I drove six hours with a podcast I did not hear. Monday I emailed the rental company, not to punish Tasha, to flag their log as an alibi. They refunded me anyway. I paid a locksmith for my apartment. Evan texted paragraphs. I answered once: the coffee was too sweet because you were practicing on someone else. I told our couple friends with the log photo, not the lipstick. Two people said they had wondered about the cologne. I bought a mug that does not match our registry set. Sometimes I write 4:10 p.m. on a sticky note and throw it away. Stupid ritual. It works.

social.description: The car on the gravel was not a coincidence and the log was not housekeeping. I left the ChapStick on the binder and drove six hours. Would you have emailed the rental company?
